subject: Post-demo recap: pricing & monthly burn calibration / procurement readiness
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@brightai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo recap: pricing & monthly burn calibration / procurement readiness

Claire — thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our call and suggested next steps so we have alignment internally and with Procurement/Finance: 

Summary of what you shared
- Primary workload: mult-turn customer support summarization + dynamic reranking for 500–900 active sessions/day.
- Expected token profile: ~10–25k tokens per session depending on context-window usage.
- Rough monthly consumption band (estimate): 40M — 150M tokens. (You mentioned high season could push toward the upper end.)

Cost / unit economics discussed
- BrightAI target target: looking to keep platform spend within a predictable range. You asked for a target price around $/1M tokens to validate budget buckets. 
- From our initial sizing, two candidate unit-cost targets make sense for discussion:
  * Pay-as-you-go list: $3,500 per 1M tokens (baseline for current verified model variants)
  * Committed/Reserved (12-month) guidance: ~$2,900 per 1M tokens (volume & commitment-dependent)
- Using those bands, monthly spend approximation:
  * Lower band (40M): $140k (pay-as-you-go) / $116k (reserved)
  * Upper band (150M): $525k / $435k

Procurement & timeline signals
- Procurement thresholds you shared: POs needed for any vendor spend > $100k; Finance prefers a single quote + SOW for review.
- Typical legal/PO lead time at BrightAI: 3–5 weeks once SOW and quote are in hand.

Asks / next steps (proposed)
1) I will follow up with a lightweight pricing matrix (paygo vs 12mo commit tiers) plus a short SOW draft for your finance team to review — aiming to capture the $/1M token bands and a simple table mapping monthly burn to monthly invoice ranges.
2) Can you confirm the internal procurement contact and whether a PO threshold exception is possible for an initial pilot (we could keep the first month below $100k if that helps)?
3) Would you like a short technical call on batching/caching strategies (15–20m) for your infra lead; that usually helps lower the unit cost materially once we tune KV caching and prefix reuse.

Attachments referenced: pricing-matrix-20270629.pdf (will attach in follow-up), SOW_draft_v1.docx (draft).

Thanks — I’ll send the matrix and SOW by EOD tomorrow.

— Soojin
Soojin Lee
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0172

From: Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@brightai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mike Torres <mike.torres@brightai.com>
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: pricing & monthly burn calibration / procurement readiness

Thanks Soojin — helpful recap. Quick clarifications: 
- The 40M number is conservative for our steady state, but we should plan for 120–150M in Q4.
- Procurement contact: I’ll loop in our vendor manager (I can introduce via email) but for now please assume PO threshold is strict at $100k; we can request an exception but it’s not guaranteed.

Can you: 
1) Send a simple 2x2 pricing matrix (paygo vs commit) showing $/1M and monthly spend estimates at 50M / 100M / 150M tokens.
2) Share the draft SOW and any standard security addendum (SOC2 evidence pointers are fine).

We’d like a clear path for a pilot that keeps the first monthly invoice <= $100k if possible. If reserved pricing requires a 12mo commitment that pushes us above that threshold, we may still do a smaller pilot then convert.

Claire
Claire Barnes
VP Product — BrightAI
claire.barnes@brightai.com

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 1 Jul 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: pricing & monthly burn calibration / procurement readiness

Quick internal note — strategy and concessions: 
- Goal: keep pilot under $100k invoice while protecting margin and positioning a clear path to reserved commit.
- Proposal: Offer a two-phased commercial path: 
  Phase A (pilot): 1 month pay-as-you-go invoice target capped at $95k. Includes 30% discount on list paygo rates for the pilot only (to get them through procurement gate).
  Phase B (conversion): 12-month reserved commitment where we drop to $2,900 / 1M tokens (provided they commit to a 9–12 month minimum consumption corridor; exact banding TO BE DETERMINED).
- Rationale: pilot discount buys time for procurement + gives us ability to onboard and measure prefix reuse / batching benefits (should reduce effective cost).

Operational asks for Sales ops / Solutions:
- Soojin: Prepare pricing matrix with Pilot capped scenario and committed scenario; include invoice examples at 50/100/150M.
- Lauren: Please prepare a short SOW template with delivery milestones, and include a checkbox for "security evidence packet (SOC2) attached".

I think this will get past the PO threshold while leaving room to convert.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.ai>
To: Claire Barnes <claire.barnes@brightai.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 2 Jul 2027 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap: pricing & monthly burn calibration / procurement readiness

Claire — looping back with the items we discussed. Attached: pricing-matrix-20270629.pdf (simple table with paygo vs pilot-cap price vs committed tiers) and SOW_draft_v1.docx (one page SOW + milestones). Highlights below to make it scannable for Finance/Procurement: 

Pricing highlights
- Pilot (1 month, capped invoice): list paygo rates with a one-time pilot discount so projected invoice at 50M tokens = $95,000 (we can include line: "invoice cap: $95k for pilot month").
- Committed (12mo): $2,900 / 1M tokens baseline for commitments >= 6 months with a consumption corridor (details in attached matrix).
- We also included an "opt-in" bandwidth adjustment clause so if they exceed 150M consistently we will reprice in good faith at quarter boundary.

Procurement & attachments
- SOW_draft_v1.docx — short statement of work, 3 milestones (integration, pilot validation, production handoff).
- Security: quick SOC2 pointer included in the SOW (we can share the full packet once the NDA/PO path is agreed).

Next steps
1) Claire / Mike: Please confirm procurement contact and whether Finance will accept a capped pilot invoice. If yes we’ll prepare final quote and send to your vendor manager.
2) If helpful, we can schedule a 20m technical sync on Monday to walk the infra lead through batching/prefix reuse to set realistic ramp expectations.

Thanks — attaching both files now.

Attachments:
- pricing-matrix-20270629.pdf (application/pdf, 46 KB)
- SOW_draft_v1.docx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document, 18 KB)

Best,
— Soojin
